messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty — page fired: INC-4521 — 5xx spike on /v1/generate (eu-1). Paging SRE rotation. Link: https://pagerduty.example/INC-4521

Alex Choi: acked and taking. oncall status -> I’m on the bridge. pulling logs now.

Devon Li: noted, standing by for handoff if needed.

Alex Choi: quick triage: errors look like `UpstreamReadError` from embedding-service. 503s cluster-wide in eu-1 for the last 2m. traffic spike?

Maria Gonzalez: are customers hitting this or internal traffic? any sensitive customers affected?

Alex Choi: customer-facing — ramped to ~2% error rate for realtime customers in EU. small subset of requests fail early (tokenize stage). tagging CS and Support.

OpsBot: Automated diagnostics started: collecting pod logs, tailing 1m, grabbing recent autoscaler events. artifacts: s3://redwood-incidents/INC-4521/

OpsBot: Quick metrics snapshot:
- 5xx rate: 1.9% -> 3.2% in 30s
- p99 latency eu-1: 420ms -> 980ms
- embedding-service pods (eu-1): 4/6 ready

SRE-Oncall: paste of relevant logs:
```
embedding-service-7c9f7d: 2026-03-15T15:01:22Z ERROR UpstreamReadError: upstream closed connection
embedding-service-7c9f7d: 2026-03-15T15:01:23Z WARN OOM? allocating kv cache failed
embedding-service-2a4b1c: 2026-03-15T15:01:24Z ERROR grpc: received RST_STREAM
```

Alex Choi: hmm looks like memory pressure on a subset of hosts. I’m ssh-ing into node eu1-n10 to check dmesg and container OOMs.

Devon Li: while you do that I’ll spin up a temporary scale (scaling to 8 pods) and enable prefix cache fallback for the route to reduce load.

Alex Choi: good plan. runbook step 3: scale pods then toggle cache fallback. runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embedding-service#memory-fallback

Devon Li: running command now:
```bash
kubectl scale deployment/embedding-service -n prod --replicas=8 --context=eu-1
```

OpsBot: kube event: scaling started for embedding-service -> target 8 replicas.

Alex Choi: ssh session: seeing repeated OOM kills on container PID 1 on eu1-n10. kernel OOM killer invoked for process `embedding-worker`. cgroup memory limit at 100% for that host.

Maria Gonzalez: flagged as potentially degradational for SLA. opening escalation to infra lead. @Devon Li please coordinate DB/redis side checks too? sometimes eviction cascade from redis causes this.

Devon Li: on it — checking redis metrics and eviction rate.

SRE-Oncall: temporary mitigation idea: route 20% of eu traffic to eu-2 region (failover) and enable degraded-mode (quantized model) for realtime customers. we can do graceful routing via router config.

Alex Choi: I’m going to hand off to Devon — I need to jump to a customer call. Devon, please confirm once routing change is live. handing off at 15:02 UTC.

Devon Li: taking over. scaling completed, pods now 8/8 ready in eu-1-ish but old hosts still have oom churn. initiating routing change to shift 20% -> eu-2 and enable quantized fallback for /v1/generate for realtime route.

Devon Li: router change (apply):
```yaml
- name: eu-realtime-route
  default: eu-1
  weighted:
    eu-1: 80
    eu-2: 20
```

OpsBot: Router apply succeeded. traffic shift in-progress.

SRE-Oncall: PG: Please post the curl health check and error rate after routing change.

Devon Li: health check (post-shift):
```bash
curl -sS https://eu-1.health/v1/ready | jq .status
# eu-1: degraded
curl -sS https://eu-2.health/v1/ready | jq .status
# eu-2: healthy
```
Error rate dropped to 0.4% overall across EU after shift. p99 latency back to ~480ms.

Alex Choi: :thumbsup: great. customer impact reduced. notifying CS with current mitigation and ETA for full fix.

Maria Gonzalez: posting to support channel now and tagging top customers in EU with transient degradation note.

pagerbot: PagerDuty update: INC-4521 escalated to L2 (infra) due to OOM evidence.

Devon Li: follow-up actions: replace bad hosts in eu-1 (kernel tuning + increase container memory limit), investigate root cause of KV cache leak, add alert to watch for container OOM kills in embedding-service. ETA for full remediation ~1.5h.

SRE-Oncall: can you also create a short rollback plan if scaling/routing doesn’t hold? add to the incident doc.

Devon Li: added rollback steps in the incident doc. link: https://confluence.internal/incidents/INC-4521/mitigation

Alex Choi: I’m back. Devon — all yours to drive to completion. I’ll stay on slack for questions.

Devon Li: will update every 10m or on any major state change. current status: mitigation stable, traffic split active, error rate under 0.5%.

OpsBot: scheduled snapshot of affected pods and heap dumps in s3://redwood-incidents/INC-4521/heapdumps/ for postmortem.

Maria Gonzalez: capturing customer impact metrics and list of affected tenants. prepping postmortem template.

Devon Li: final check — scaling + routing have kept the service stable for 9m. I’m going to cordon eu1-n10 and reprovision. will update when done.

pagerbot: INC-4521 acknowledged by devon via PagerDuty at 15:11 UTC; status: mitigated.

Devon Li: reprovision started. cordon + replace node eu1-n10.

Alex Choi: thanks everyone. after node replace we can gradually shift traffic back and lower replica count.

SRE-Oncall: reminder to file a short blameless postmortem and link to tickets for kernel tuning and memory limit bump.

Devon Li: incident resolved -> moving to post-incident follow-up. closing thread in 10m if no regression.

pagerbot: Incident INC-4521 marked mitigated and will be closed after follow-up tasks are created. :white_check_mark:
